content.text: This document outlines the refactoring plan for modifying the hello_world endpoint to return a random UUID and updating the search endpoint to require this UUID. Additionally, it details the necessary changes in the client code that calls these endpoints.

The current architecture includes a hello_world endpoint that does not return any data and a search endpoint that performs various operations to fetch and display search results. The client code calls these endpoints directly.

Modifying the hello_world endpoint to return a UUID ensures that each search request is associated with a unique identifier. This change will help in tracking and auditing search requests more effectively.

The existing architecture involves several functions and API calls as described in the context. The hello_world endpoint returns a JSON response, while the search_monolith endpoint performs various operations to fetch and display search results.

graph TD
  A[call_hello_world_api] -->|calls| B(/hello_world)
  C[call_search_api] -->|calls| D(search_monolith)
  D --> E(_apply_business_logic_and_filter)
  D --> F(_authenticate_user)
  D --> G(_fetch_data_from_primary_db)
  D --> H(_fetch_data_from_secondary_service)
  D --> I(_format_results_for_display)
  D --> J(_log_search_query)

The proposed architecture modifies the hello_world endpoint to return a UUID. The search_monolith endpoint is updated to require this UUID as a parameter. The client code is also modified to call the hello_world endpoint first and then use the returned UUID in the search endpoint.

Modify the hello_world endpoint in Repo1/app.py to return a random UUID.
Update the search_monolith endpoint in Repo1/app.py to accept and use a UUID parameter.
Modify the call_search_api function in Repo2/client.py to first call the hello_world endpoint and then use the returned UUID in the search endpoint.
Test the updated endpoints and client code to ensure they work as expected.
